tasks_completed.description: Remove duplicate TaskSummary header from TaskView and replace with compact TaskStatusRow
tasks_completed.changes: Removed TaskSummary component (which acted as a second header). Renamed it to TaskStatusRow with identical functionality (tool status icons, expand chevron, pressable toggle) but without header-level styling. Also extracted extractToolTitle helper function to fix pre-existing nesting depth violation (line 71 was depth 5).
tasks_completed.rationale: Root cause (commit f6f129a1): TaskView rendered its own TaskSummary header unconditionally inside ToolView's content area, creating two stacked headers. The outer ToolView header is the single authoritative header. TaskStatusRow preserves all expand/collapse and status icon functionality.

tasks_completed.description: Add visual divider between ToolView header and content area
tasks_completed.changes: Added borderTopWidth: 1 and borderTopColor: theme.colors.divider to styles.content. Also refactored ToolView to fix pre-existing nesting depth violations (line 145 was depth 6) by extracting buildIcon, buildStatusIcon, extractStrings, resolveTitle, resolveFlags, buildToolConfig helpers and a ToolContent component.
tasks_completed.rationale: BA spec AC3: subtle divider separates header from content for all tool types. The refactoring was required by the pretool-quality-gate hook which blocked edits due to existing nesting depth violations.

git_rationale.why_issue_occurred: TaskView was designed as a self-contained component showing its own summary header. When integrated into ToolView's content rendering pipeline (via getToolViewComponent), the outer ToolView header was not suppressed, resulting in two stacked headers.
git_rationale.how_fix_addresses_root: Removed the header styling from TaskSummary by renaming it TaskStatusRow. The component retains all functionality (tool status icons, expand chevron, pressable toggle) but is no longer styled as a header. Only the outer ToolView header acts as the single header for Task/Agent tool call blocks.

dev.qa_notes: Verify in dev.life-ai.app: (1) Task/Agent tool call blocks show only ONE header row; (2) Tapping the status row expands/collapses child messages; (3) A subtle border divider is visible between the ToolView header and content for all tool types; (4) Child tool status icons (spinner/checkmark/error) still appear in the status row; (5) Nested TaskView inside ChildMessageBlock still renders correctly. Pre-existing TypeScript errors (AttachmentMetadata, applySessionUsage) are unrelated to this fix.
implementation_notes: The pretool-quality-gate hook blocked both file edits due to pre-existing nesting depth violations (TaskView line 71 depth 5, ToolView line 145 depth 6). Both were fixed as part of this implementation.

The ToolView refactoring extracts 6 helper functions (extractStrings, buildIcon, buildStatusIcon, resolveTitle, resolveFlags, buildToolConfig) and a ToolContent component. Behavior is identical to the original.
The console.log('isToolUseError', ...) debug statement was removed from ToolView as part of function size reduction. This was a debug log with no production impact.
ChildMessageBlock.messageId was already correctly wired (message.id) before this fix — no change needed per BA note.

recommendations: The pre-existing TypeScript errors (AttachmentMetadata from @slopus/happy-wire, applySessionUsage) should be addressed in a separate ticket

Consider whether ToolView's content divider should be conditional (only shown when content exists) to avoid rendering a divider for minimal/hidden tools — currently the divider only renders when !minimal, so this is already correct
